candidate.analysis: The program reads /input/public_csv, identifies the named columns, computes fish-per-hour for each trip, summarizes sample size and mean rate, and reports Pearson correlations between the rate and available numeric predictors. It also fits a simple ordinary least-squares model for fish caught using hours, livebait, camper, persons, and child when sufficient complete data are available. Results are descriptive associations, not causal claims.
candidate.answer: Across 250 trips, visitors caught an average of 1.1074 fish per hour (median 0). The strongest observed association with catch rate was persons (correlation 0.2177); livebait (0.0643) and camper status (0.0648) were weakly positive, while child count (-0.0285) and hours spent (-0.0683) were negligible-to-weakly negative. An OLS model estimated fish caught coefficients of 0.1452 per hour, 3.2207 for livebait, 2.3362 for camper, 4.5837 per person, and -4.8675 per child. These are descriptive associations, not causal effects.
